plates.quality_reason: Flow-first: a teach diagram, chart, counter or timeline is a £0 code graphic. No Flow mint.
plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, the 3-era timeline completes: 1882–1883 & 1906 (Sidney Ringer discovers calcium-driven cardiac contraction in London tap water; Arthur Keith and Martin Flack discover the sinoatrial node pacemaker in Kent) · 1901–1903 (Willem Einthoven builds the 600-pound string galvanometer in Leiden and records the P–Q–R–S–T electrocardiogram, winning the 1924 Nobel Prize) · 1956 – 7 May 1958 & 1960 (Wilson Greatbatch accidentally inserts a 1-megaohm resistor in Buffalo and with William Chardack builds the first successful multi-year implantable cardiac pacemaker).

teach_overlay.detail: Animated timeline (1882 → 1970) alongside an inked comparison of Einthoven's 270 kg string galvanometer and Greatbatch's 2-cubic-inch lithium-iodide implantable pacemaker
teach_overlay.scale: from a London tap-water mistake and a 600-pound magnet in Leiden to a single wrong resistor in a Buffalo barn, scientists learned to read and restart the electrical spark of life
